title: Orbital Pool Commander: compact control surface for GPU pool health, autoscale and burst
text:
Orbital Pool Commander: compact control surface for GPU pool health, autoscale and burst

description:
Design a compact, single-pane control surface for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces health, recent anomalies, autoscaling policy controls, and burst configuration. The goal is to reduce operator cognitive load during platform incidents and make safe tuning accessible to product and ops users without exposing low-level infra jargon.

design_goals:
Show top-of-page health snapshot (SLOs, utilization, queue length) with single-number indicators and micro-trends
Expose autoscale policy quick-actions (enable/disable, target concurrency, cooldown) inline with safe defaults
Provide an explicit burst workflow with predicted cost delta and rollback path
Avoid deep navigation: single surface for triage -> act -> validate
Mobile-friendly compact layout for on-call use

acceptance_criteria:
Prototype includes health snapshot, autoscale quick-actions, burst editor, and recent incidents feed
Design tokens follow Console v2 (spacing, color scale, typography) and accessible contrast levels
Embedded cost estimation tooltip for burst with clear assumptions and link to billing dashboard
Usability test (n=6) shows operators can complete: (1) identify degraded pool, (2) increase burst by 1 GPU type, (3) rollback an autoscale change within 2 minutes
Design handed off with annotated Figma frames and a small spec doc for engineering implementation

review_notes:
03/06 - PM (Arjun Patel): prefer a read-only 'predicted cost' preview before committing burst; requested retained history for last 7 days
03/08 - Eng (Sofia Alvarez): raised question about autoscale cooldown controls mapping to backend API v2; flagged need for minimal API surface for quick-actions
03/09 - Security (Ethan Brooks): requested that burst changes require an audit-log entry and optional approval flow for enterprise orgs
03/10 - Design critique: recommend collapsing 'queue length' into the utilization microtrend to save vertical space for mobile
03/11 - Usability session (internal ops): testers confused by 'soft-burst' vs 'hard-burst' terminology; decision to rename to 'temporary burst' and 'reserved burst'

decisions:
Rename burst types to 'temporary burst' and 'reserved burst' across UI
Include a cost-preview flyout with assumptions (GPU type, duration, estimated tokens) shown before applying burst
Autoscale quick-actions will call a single 'policy-adjust' API with minimal fields: target_concurrency, cooldown_seconds, reason
Burst changes will create an audit log entry and, if org has enterprise approval enabled, surface an approval modal
Compact layout chosen (three stacked cards) to prioritize triage-first workflow

next_steps:
Revise Figma frames to replace 'soft/hard' labels with new terminology (by 2026-03-13) - Maya
Work with Eng (Sofia) to map UI controls to API v2 contract and surface validation errors inline (by 2026-03-15)
Prepare 6-run usability script for external ops team and book sessions (target week of 2026-03-22)
Add billing link and cost-presets to prototype and re-run cost clarity check
Create engineering handoff doc with token-level animations and acceptance criteria
